prompt: `search` had `nodeSelector: {disk: ssd}` and three replicas. Where did they run?
hint: Only one node carried the label.

choices.why: Right, even with `shop-worker` idle.
The selector excludes every node without the label.
A requirement never sends a pod elsewhere.

choices.text: Nowhere, until a second node was labelled
choices.why: One labelled node was enough for all three.

prompt: After the selector was changed to `disk: nvme`, the three old `search` pods kept running. Why?
hint: What does a rollout do before removing an old pod?

choices.text: Selectors only apply to new Deployments
choices.why: The new pod did get the new selector.
kubectl answered `patched`.

choices.text: The new pod never started, so the rollout stopped
choices.why: Right. Old pods go only as new ones become ready.

choices.text: The old pods moved to an nvme node
choices.why: No node had `disk=nvme`, and pods never move.

prompt: `cache` preferred `disk` in `[nvme, ssd]` with weight 100. What would have happened if `shop-worker2` had been full?

choices.why: That is what a requirement does.
Right. Preferred rules add points; they forbid nothing.

choices.text: The scheduler would evict other pods
choices.why: Preferences never trigger eviction.
Placement is decided after the object is accepted.

prompt: A running pod was placed by `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` on a node labelled `disk=ssd`. Someone removes the label. What happens to the pod?
hint: Read the end of the field's name.

choices.why: The rule is ignored during execution.

choices.text: It is restarted on another node
choices.why: Pods never move.
A running pod cannot return to `Pending`.
Right. The rule is checked only when the pod is placed.

prompt: With required anti-affinity on `kubernetes.io/hostname` and three replicas, why did one `shop` pod stay `Pending`?
hint: How many nodes take ordinary pods?

choices.text: The image was missing on one node
choices.why: The event named anti-affinity and a taint.

choices.text: Anti-affinity limits a Deployment to two pods
choices.why: It limits pods per domain, not per Deployment.

choices.text: The nodes ran out of CPU
choices.why: The event said nothing about resources.

choices.text: Two usable nodes each held a copy
choices.why: Right, and the control plane is tainted.

prompt: Which `topologyKey` makes anti-affinity keep copies in different zones rather than different nodes?

choices.why: That domain is one node.
Right. Each zone becomes one domain.
That groups nodes by operating system.
That is a pod label, not a node domain.
